newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Uncertainty dogs SAfrica oil sector - Engen.
newsitem.headline: Uncertainty dogs SAfrica oil sector - Engen.

text.p: Uncertainty over the deregulation of the South African oil industry placed companies in a difficult position, Engen Ltd chairman Bernard Smith said on Tuesday.
"These issues are complex and it will take a substantial amount of goodwill on the part of everyone involved in order to ensure a successful outcome," Smith told the group's annual general meeting.
In particular, the industry awaited a response from government on its application for a three cents a litre increase in the wholesale marketing margin paid to oil companies.

But even without this increase, Smith said that Engen expected to increase net income in the current year although much would depend on international refining margins and crude prices and the rand-dollar exchange rate.
He said that international refining margins had narrowed in the first quarter of the current year, crude prices were well above the 1996 year-end level and the rand continued weak.
One of the major challenges facing the group was improving the performance of its Durban refinery.

"Particular attention is being focused on the visbreaker, as being the unit mainly responsible for impeding improvements to white oil yields, which remain at levels similar to the 1996 financial year average," Smith said.
On subsidiary Energy Africa, Smith said results from recent drilling activities in Angola, Congo and Namibia were now being evaluated.
"Development studies are already in progress on block 2/92 in Angola, and Energy Africa is confident that production will commence within the next two years," Smith said.
In a joint venture with Norwegian Independent Saga, Energy Africa had also bid on a deep water block offshore Angola and the results were expected in early 1997.
Energy Africa planned to drill a further eight to 10 well during 1997, Smith said.
The benefits of the link-up with Malaysian oil company Petronas were expected to start being realised in 1997, "particularly in the areas of logistics and business ventures," he said.
